Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Wed Oct 28 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Vance, located a couple hundred miles west-southwest of Cabo
Corrientes, Mexico.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Public Advisory Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Wed Oct 28 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 281432
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Vance Advisory Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 AM MST Wed Oct 28 2026
 
...VANCE REMAINS A HIGHLY SHEARED TROPICAL STORM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.2N 109.2W
ABOUT 320 MI...515 KM W OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 240 MI...390 KM WSW OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 340 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests along the west-central and northwestern coasts of Mexico
and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the
progress of Vance.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Vance was
located near latitude 19.2 North, longitude 109.2 West. Vance is
moving toward the north-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A turn 
toward the north and north-northeast is expected later today and 
tonight, with the center passing to the west of Islas Marias 
overnight. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast today, followed by gradual 
weakening tonight through Friday. Vance is expected to become a 
post-tropical remnant low on Thursday.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 90 miles (150 km)
from the center in the eastern semicircle.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
RAINFALL: Through Thursday, Vance is expected to produce 2 to 4
inches of rain across central and southern Sinaloa, far southwestern
Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, with isolated higher totals
of 7 inches possible over central and southern Sinaloa. This
rainfall may produce flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
along steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Vance,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf.
 
SURF: Swells generated by Vance will affect coastal portions of
southwestern and west-central Mexico, as well as the southern
portion of the Baja California Peninsula during the next couple of
days. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Tropical Storm Vance Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Wed Oct 28 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 281433
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Vance Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP222026
800 AM MST Wed Oct 28 2026
 
After a robust convective burst overnight, the low-level center of 
Vance is now fully exposed once again as strong westerly shear 
persists over the storm. The lingering convective activity is 
displaced well to the east of Vance's center, with gusty winds and 
heavy rain spreading toward Islas Marias and coastal portions of 
west-central Mexico. The initial intensity is held at 35 kt, which 
is supported by the latest TAFB Dvorak classification, UW-CIMSS 
objective estimates, and the overnight scatterometer data.

The long-term motion of Vance is to the north-northwest (340/9 kt), 
although the exposed center has moved erratically this morning. 
Recent satellite images suggest Vance is beginning to turn more 
northward as expected, and the track models agree on a northward to 
north-northeastward motion during the next couple of days. The 
latest NHC forecast lies to the left of the previous one, mainly the 
result of an initial westward position adjustment. The vertical wind 
shear over Vance will remain very strong during the next 24-48 
hours, and simulated satellite imagery from the GFS and ECMWF show 
the system devoid of convection by tomorrow morning. The updated NHC 
forecast shows Vance becoming a post-tropical remnant low in 24 
hours, with continued weakening through Friday that follows HCCA and 
IVCN. It is possible that the remnant low dissipates over the Gulf 
of California before it reaches the coast of Mexico.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Periods of heavy rainfall associated with Vance will impact 
portions of western Mexico during much of this week. This rainfall 
may produce flooding and mudslides across central and southern 
Sinaloa, far southwestern Durango, and far northwestern Nayarit, 
especially in areas along steep terrain.
 
2. Interests along the west-central and northwestern coasts of 
Mexico and the southern Baja California Peninsula should monitor the 
progress of Vance.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  28/1500Z 19.2N 109.2W   35 KT  40 MPH
 12H  29/0000Z 20.6N 109.0W   35 KT  40 MPH
 24H  29/1200Z 22.2N 108.6W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  30/0000Z 23.9N 108.2W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  30/1200Z 24.9N 108.2W   20 KT  25 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 60H  31/0000Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart
